newsitem.title: USA: FBI conducts searches in computer child porn probe.
newsitem.headline: FBI conducts searches in computer child porn probe.

text.p: The FBI said Wednesday it had conducted searches in 20 cities as part of a continuing nationwide crackdown on child pornography involving computer online services and the Internet.

FBI officials said the search warrants were executed at the homes of suspected child pornography users, and arrests were expected as part of the three-year investigation, dubbed "Operation Innocent Images."
"These crimes, preying on innocent children, represent every parent's worst nightmare," FBI Director Louis Freeh said in a statement.
"These cases have already revealed the ease and frequency with which criminals have used modern technology to cause grave harm to children," he said.

The searches were conducted by FBI offices in Albany, New York, Albuquerque, Baltimore, Boston, Charlotte, Cincinnati, Denver, Milwaukee, Newark, Oklahoma City, Pittsburgh, Richmond, Sacramento, Tampa and Washington, D.C.

The investigation began after the 1993 disappearance of George Burdynski, a 10-year-old boy from Brentwood, Maryland. The investigation revealed that computers were being used to lure minors into sexual conduct and send child pornography.

The FBI's undercover investigation, which was run out of its Baltimore office and publicly disclosed in September last year, has resulted so far in 80 arrests, 66 convictions and more than 200 searches.
